03f0276d-ea71-550e-87b2-3e9d039d58d4.name: Amor and Psyche – Garden
03f0276d-ea71-550e-87b2-3e9d039d58d4.description: During the first stage of the construction of the chateau a park, in the style of French Baroque gardens, was taking shape outside the west wing under the guidance of Dutch experts. The garden casino with Lanzani’s decoration and a fountain by Peter Wiliame, has not survived and only the romantic Chinese pavilion from the 1780s remains. In the mid-19th century the garden, covering 15 hectares, was simplified in the “English” style. A reconstruction in the 1970s partially restored the Baroque appearance of the chateau parterre with pools and fountains and re-installed the mythological and allegorical stone figures.

059edbc5-9442-564e-ae32-2efb3b02e0ba.name: Benediction Room
059edbc5-9442-564e-ae32-2efb3b02e0ba.description:
The Benediction Room at the centre of the royal palace appears to be part of the Basilica as it has the same polychrome marble decoration.  
It symbolises the divine origins of Absolute Kingship, to whose authority even the Church submitted. From this room over the Basilica, the Royal Family attended mass, and from the veranda (on the opposite side) opening onto the square, King João V blessed his subjects.
059edbc5-9442-564e-ae32-2efb3b02e0ba.location: In the middle of the Royal Palace

091b9985-830d-5a24-aeb3-8b6403f919cf.name: St. Paulo Obelisk Fountain
091b9985-830d-5a24-aeb3-8b6403f919cf.description: From the Mãe d' Água das Amoreiras, a secondary aqueduct spreads out around the city terminating in fountains, many of them like this one still extant. Designed by Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos in 1774, it was not built until 1848, with minor adaptations by Malaquias Ferreira Leal.
091b9985-830d-5a24-aeb3-8b6403f919cf.artist: Design: Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos [n.d.]; adapted by Malaquias Ferreira Leal (1790–1855)

092d3c2e-305d-5a72-89a2-85afc05e6e72.name: *Allegory of Fortune, of Love and of the Four Seasons*
092d3c2e-305d-5a72-89a2-85afc05e6e72.description: Charged by Marc’Antonio Ranuzzi, Marc’Antonio Franceschini and the quadratura painter Enrico Haffner realized the allegorical figures in the ceiling of this room on the first floor of the palace, presumably between 1680 and 1681. Very interesting and original is the allegory in the centre of the vault showing Fortune and her wheel which, moved by the wind, holds Cupid in chains.
092d3c2e-305d-5a72-89a2-85afc05e6e72.location: Ceiling decoration of a room of the first floor of the palace, Palazzo Ranuzzi

0f34fb84-1a32-5e05-bab6-63b99f2384be.name: Allegory of Beneficent Reign
0f34fb84-1a32-5e05-bab6-63b99f2384be.description: An *Allegory of Beneficent Reign* observes the governor's decisions from above his throne. The original vaulting acquired the symbolic function of a “triumphal arch”. D. Gran was an exponent of Vienna academicism, well versed in producing iconographic programmes on given subjects. Gran's decoration of the Court Library in Vienna inspired M. O. Kounic to commission him rather tha Brno artists Etgens and Eckstein; B. Altomonte also tendered for the commission. Together with the quadraturist G. Fanti, Gran created a mural in the Assembly Hall that sealed his reputation as one of the most sought-after fresco artists of the first half of the 18th century. Several surviving sketches demonstrate the artist's careful preparation for the commission.

11ba5be2-9ef2-554a-855f-c08f25e2d190.name: Gate
11ba5be2-9ef2-554a-855f-c08f25e2d190.description: The triumphal arch with a triangular gable separates the chateau from the town. The original connection by means of the triumphal path was broken and emphasis placed on vistas. The family’s coat of arms is surrounded by the mottos “Kindness is not forgotten” and “the lustre of faith outlasts even a rock”.

14cf3ac9-f201-5ffe-96c6-9da83f2f8352.name: Library Façade
14cf3ac9-f201-5ffe-96c6-9da83f2f8352.description: Magnificent Baroque façade in limestone with four huge columns crowned by the royal coat of arms and the phrase “So highly are books praised here in Coimbra that a library crowns the city head”.

178756de-2fc7-5c0f-9aeb-af17d4b308f4.name: Diana, Goddess of the Hunt
178756de-2fc7-5c0f-9aeb-af17d4b308f4.description: In accordance with the use of the Amalienburg as a hunting lodge, the stuccoed overdoor of the main portal facing the garden depicts Diana, goddess of the hunt, as a half figure, surrounded with putti, hounds and hunting equipment.
178756de-2fc7-5c0f-9aeb-af17d4b308f4.location: Niche above the central portal of the eastern façade

1a5ad99e-4e60-596e-9113-8c0b78eebfe2.name: Large reading tables
1a5ad99e-4e60-596e-9113-8c0b78eebfe2.description: The six large tables (buffets) in multi-coloured and exotic woods are all slightly different and designed to match each room.
1a5ad99e-4e60-596e-9113-8c0b78eebfe2.location: Interior, Biblioteca Joanina da Universidade de Coimbra

1b76ee67-59f5-5426-ae90-e4aff6200791.name: Electress’s Private Chapel
1b76ee67-59f5-5426-ae90-e4aff6200791.description: Panelled with scagliola marble, the chapel flaunts its sumptuous ornamental decoration. To great effect, the ceiling, decorated with interlacing stuccowork, opens into an oval lantern displaying a fresco of heaven. The valuable altarpiece comes from the workshop of Peter Paul Rubens.
1b76ee67-59f5-5426-ae90-e4aff6200791.location: New Palace, first floor of the north wing

1e1c41cd-e203-5847-9534-cb31a2f69f12.name: Monumental staircase
1e1c41cd-e203-5847-9534-cb31a2f69f12.description: The monumental staircase has a complex structure, based on an elliptical plan. Two large flights of stairs embrace, rising, the area where the stair is placed; one more flight rises in the opposite direction driving to the first floor. From the balconies all around it is possible to observe the very suggestive and dynamic development of the stair, where reality and fiction are mixed up thanks to the illusive use of paintings by Ercole Graziani. Many years later Filippo Balugani realized the sculptures representing pagan gods that are placed over the balustrades.
1e1c41cd-e203-5847-9534-cb31a2f69f12.artist: Giovanni Battista Torri; Carlo Fontana; Ercole Graziani; Filippo Balugani

1ed39711-b2cf-5d1f-b9ad-2e38cdf83f46.name: Plague Column
1ed39711-b2cf-5d1f-b9ad-2e38cdf83f46.description: The column, crowned by the Virgin Mary vanquisher of evil, was erected in gratitude to the end of the plague epidemic. It was among the first columns of its kind in Moravia.

205ab685-f8e2-5231-8359-9f897f061f3f.name: Glory of Moravia
205ab685-f8e2-5231-8359-9f897f061f3f.description: An obelisk, symbol of eternity, carries the emblem of Moravia. The upper section of the main element of the ceiling painting features a zodiac, the eternal cycle of time. The personifications of the sun and moon at the sides accentuate the eternal validity of the central slogan being unfurled by Fame.

24ec6e48-1e49-57da-8b31-cb3cc3c40a0c.name: Muse
24ec6e48-1e49-57da-8b31-cb3cc3c40a0c.description: The quadrature contains figures of the Muses, without whose help fame and prosperity are unthinkable. The detail shows the engraved under-drawing.
24ec6e48-1e49-57da-8b31-cb3cc3c40a0c.artist: Daniel Gran (1694 Vienna – 1757 St. Pölten), Gaetano Fanti (1687 Bologna – 1759 Vienna)

28637f70-e837-5910-a49b-bc2c9584b6d0.name: View of the Sanctuary
28637f70-e837-5910-a49b-bc2c9584b6d0.description: Late Baroque synthesis of a longitudinal and central space.

2eb1f102-370e-5a15-aa76-966aead4921b.name: Ceiling fresco of the Great Hall
2eb1f102-370e-5a15-aa76-966aead4921b.description: The ceiling fresco of the Great Hall was once the world’s largest. Illustrating the fight between Aeneas and Turnus for the hand of the king’s daughter Lavinia, Aeneas, it is sometimes said resembles the Elector Max II Emanuel. The use of a painted landscape background instead of *trompe-l’oeil* architectural decoration was novel at the time.
2eb1f102-370e-5a15-aa76-966aead4921b.location: New Palace, first floor of the central wing

2f3b7be6-81ba-55c8-a553-1e425e26df8b.name: Cupola painting of the crossing
2f3b7be6-81ba-55c8-a553-1e425e26df8b.description: The large, circular dome fresco is surrounded by four stucco cartouches with pictures of the evangelists that show the wonder of Whitsun and its meaning for the worldwide mission of the church. The architectural scenery of the step-platforms, balustrades and surrounding obelisks is typical of the art of *mise en scène* used for composing ceiling paintings.
2f3b7be6-81ba-55c8-a553-1e425e26df8b.location: Crossing vault of the abbey church

31a2ed6c-a768-5550-a180-6fecff19b3b0.name: Exterior, south façade
31a2ed6c-a768-5550-a180-6fecff19b3b0.description: Designed by Gumpp in 1754, the Hofgasse Wing was completed according to his plans by 1756. The centre of the wing is composed of a monumental portal projection in the form of a gabled triumphal arch encompassing all four storeys. It is only here that Johann Martin Gumpp’s façade conception has been realised completely in accordance with his ideas. The influence of his brother Georg Anton’s country house façade is evident. The ponderous Late Baroque style has been adjusted to contemporary taste with the addition of rocaille work on the windows.

31a85a61-1ef8-530b-8b89-bfb3cb6f169d.name: Memorial Chapel for Emperor Franz I
31a85a61-1ef8-530b-8b89-bfb3cb6f169d.description: On the order of Maria Theresa the room in which the emperor died in August 1765 was converted into a memorial chapel by Pacassi and an endowment for ladies of rank was founded in his honour. The hall, structured with pilasters, is adorned with gentle rocaille stucco of which the tribune features a painted relief group of God the Father with mourning angels from Franz Anton Leitensdorffer (1721–95).

37077acc-2bd2-556b-ada4-0cdd3f56fffb.name: Rua das Amoreiras Arch
37077acc-2bd2-556b-ada4-0cdd3f56fffb.description: Thanks to the architectural risk-taking of Carlos Mardel, the Rua das Amoreiras arch was built between 1746 and 1748. Two things make this monumental structure particularly notable: its innovation, for over the final perpendicular branch of the aqueduct the water galleries from Alcântara run and this had never before been seen; and the engineering – from here the aqueduct turns sharp right to the Mãe d'Água reservoir. The Amoreiras Arch frames the Rua das Amoreiras and represented at one time an “entrance”, as if it were an arch in a defensive wall, highlighting both the exceptional status of this hydraulic masterpiece and its setting.

3872b95b-f605-5d55-a762-172880091112.name: The Good Government of Urban VIII
3872b95b-f605-5d55-a762-172880091112.description: The Good Government of Urban VIII, with Dignity in the centre flanked on the left by Prudence and on the right by the Delegated Power which receives a letter and is preparing to leave on a mission; on the left, the Forge of Vulcan, and on the right Peace and Fame.

38ad57d4-b61f-536a-8b64-9601d38d1e4e.name: Courtyard
38ad57d4-b61f-536a-8b64-9601d38d1e4e.description: The ceremonial courtyard is closed off by low out-buildings joined by the entrance gate. In the frontage, by the entrance to the chateau, are allegorical female figures bearing the coats of arms of the Sinzendorfs and Valdštejns. Archduke Friedrich of Habsburg demolished the existing fortifications, filled the moats and reconstructed the chateau in the Empire style. Parts of the side wings of the ceremonial courtyard were lowered and the frontages unified in a Neo-Baroque style. The statues of Saints Anne and Joachim, along with the Virgin Mary and St. Joseph, originally adorned the chapel entrance.

3a82940b-0422-54ce-94e9-7b0610d5dd16.name: Cupola
3a82940b-0422-54ce-94e9-7b0610d5dd16.description: This was the first cupola built in Portugal, similar to that of St. Peter’s in Rome. Sixty-two metres high, it is marble outside and with polychrome marble inside. The cupola has an eight-sided form and eight windows, above which are the sculpted litanies of the Virgin Mary. Forty-one men worked simultaneously on the decoration “very well and at ease”, according to a testimony in contemporary sources.

3d279afa-014f-54de-b5b3-c820b9b5e080.name: Grand Hall
3d279afa-014f-54de-b5b3-c820b9b5e080.description: The most significant and artistically most important room in the building is the Grand Hall on the second floor, designed after the fire of 1785. Stucco decorations on the walls imitate grey marble with dark veins, while at one time those of the vault were painted light yellow. Architectural decoration powerfully articulates the surfaces.
3d279afa-014f-54de-b5b3-c820b9b5e080.location: Second floor, Palace of the Sugar Refinery

4538f38d-a64f-5f64-ba07-d2b5bab3e669.name: Riesensaal
4538f38d-a64f-5f64-ba07-d2b5bab3e669.description: The “Riesensaal”, whose name is derived from an earlier cycle of Hercules paintings, together with the court chapel, is the second room dedicated to the memory of Emperor Franz I and designed according to the model of the Grand Gallery in Schönbrunn Palace. The banqueting hall extending across the whole width of the wing on Rennweg encompasses two storeys and seven window axes. It is furnished in honour of the House of Habsburg. The huge fresco panels depict allegories, the oil paintings the family of the imperial couple.

46bb4fb6-c314-5cbe-a7dc-30c998b1dfb1.name: Garden frontage
46bb4fb6-c314-5cbe-a7dc-30c998b1dfb1.description: The garden was designed as part of the chateau reconstruction. The French architect, Charbonier, worked on the site in 1714–15. The chateau frontage opened onto the garden through a terrace with a three-shouldered staircase with statues that also decorated the garden. Today they are found in the niches of the stereotomous frontage with sharp linear elements. The axis parterre was lined by double pathways and the chateau was encircled by a moat. The garden, with a conservatory, was considered one of the most beautiful in the country. The local gardener, Hatzl, was summoned to the court of Maria Theresa and put in charge of the Schönbrunn gardens in Vienna. The first hot-air balloon in Moravia was launched outside the Židlochovice Chateau in 1784.
46bb4fb6-c314-5cbe-a7dc-30c998b1dfb1.artist: Ernst August Charbonnier (1677–1747 Hannover?), Ludwig Sebastian Kaltner

4794de30-313e-53cb-8def-1b482c7a40ea.name: *Sanguinic*
4794de30-313e-53cb-8def-1b482c7a40ea.location: Wall of the working cabinet, Ratkaj Palace

4bdace62-bc43-503d-9780-29b787d8dbe1.name: Hall of Mirrors
4bdace62-bc43-503d-9780-29b787d8dbe1.description: As the heart of the small palace , the Hall of Mirrors functioned as a ballroom, concert hall or as a place of relaxation for the court society following a hunt. Mirrors inside the hall are applied to the wall sections between the windows. The interplay of real and reflecting windows appears to dissolve the surface of the walls and blurs the boundaries between the inside and the outside. The  windows and mirrors are framed with sophisticated Régence style décor and silver-plated carvings. Zimmermann's capriccio-like stuccoes of the ceiling transforms it into an Eden-like landscape by depicting trees, putti, divine figures and birds. This theme of the décor is used to connect the interior of the Amalienburg with its formerly surrounding French formal  garden.
4bdace62-bc43-503d-9780-29b787d8dbe1.artist: Design: François de Cuvilliés the Elder (1695–1768); Stucco: Johann Baptist Zimmermann (1680–1758); Ornamental carvings: Johann Joachim Dietrich (1690–1753)

4fe53e71-5945-5d6a-9e28-e7a34d244285.name: Freemasons’ Room
4fe53e71-5945-5d6a-9e28-e7a34d244285.description: The decoration of the chateau was completed in the early 19th century, in the spirit of the “spiritual alchemy” of the late Enlightenment. The Mniszeks finished the Empire-style construction of the stable frontage and made minor Neo-Gothic and Romantic adjustments to the frontages. They also built chapels, crosses, obelisks and family memorials in the park. In 1816 Stanislav Mniszek purchased a stoneware factory and turned it into a famous manufactory.

50b2d233-8179-54ab-9a65-4f12378d21af.name: Parliament hall
50b2d233-8179-54ab-9a65-4f12378d21af.description: The central hall, the parliament’s assembly hall, extends over one and a half floors and is the representative highpoint of the interior. Following the model of Italian galleries, it is situated on the second as opposed to the first floor (cf. Augsburg Town Hall). The excellent interior design work pursues the idea of the state’s political self-representation. Statues of princes and regents, attributed to Nikolaus Moll, depict Tyrol’s rulers and regents, the frescos from Asam present the state and its history in connection with biblical scenes, placing it under the protection of divine providence, the putti from Lechleitner display the symbols of the estates.
50b2d233-8179-54ab-9a65-4f12378d21af.location: Centre of the second floor in the main wing, (Old) Federal State Parliament
50b2d233-8179-54ab-9a65-4f12378d21af.artist: Georg Anton Gumpp (1682–1754); sculptural work: Ingenuin Lechleitner (1676–1731); Nikolaus Moll (1676–1754); Cosmas Damian Asam (1686–1739)

514d8dc0-868f-5204-a073-0bc44b2dabbb.name: Robillion Pavilion
514d8dc0-868f-5204-a073-0bc44b2dabbb.description: Designed by Robillion, the Pavilion is sometimes considered one of Portugal's first Neo-Classical buildings. However, it is no more than an expression of the *French* Baroque – obviously more “Classical” – attached to the overall palace form. It has two floors and a considerable monumentality, emphasised by the Stairway of the Lions.

542f882d-f0f2-5fe9-acfb-9ba0da1c097f.name: Staircase
542f882d-f0f2-5fe9-acfb-9ba0da1c097f.description: The stone cantilever staircase is decorated with sculptures of *putti* holding components of the family's coat of arms and representing allegories of the Senses. Cartouches in the parapet feature scenes from Virgil's *Aeneid*. The monumental staircase hall closes with a fresco of Odysseus presenting the Trojan horse. The entrance space portrays the family as protectors of Christianity and patrons of the arts.
542f882d-f0f2-5fe9-acfb-9ba0da1c097f.artist: Johann Christian Pröbstl, Josef Tadeáš Rotter (1701 Opava – 1763 Brno)

5581753a-eaef-56a7-aafa-55998200dcf9.name: High altar
5581753a-eaef-56a7-aafa-55998200dcf9.description: The high apse windows allow light to shine upon the imposing high altar; marble columns wind their way up into the heights, clearly alluding to the choir of the Theatine Church in Munich. Between the columns are the statues of Zacharias and Joachim as well as Anna and Elizabeth, relatives of the Virgin Mary whose Ascension to Heaven is depicted on the altarpiece. The scene develops into a sculptural medium depicting Christ recieving his mother with open arms beneath a glory of rays.
5581753a-eaef-56a7-aafa-55998200dcf9.artist: Egid Quirin Asam (1692–1750); Thomas Schaidhauf (1735–1810); Johann Nepomuk Schöpf (c. 1735–after 1785)

5718ac81-d92d-51a8-a1ec-2e1b0253d7a9.name: Theatre room
5718ac81-d92d-51a8-a1ec-2e1b0253d7a9.description: The theatre room was used for the performance of spiritual enactments.
5718ac81-d92d-51a8-a1ec-2e1b0253d7a9.location: North wing (3rd floor), Benedictine Abbey of St. Theodor and Alexander

5842aabd-e2d2-5fed-b156-c2aae539180c.name: Statues of the Founders
5842aabd-e2d2-5fed-b156-c2aae539180c.description: The two monumental statues of the founders, the Bavarian Duke Ludwig (Louis) II and his son who shared his name and was promoted to Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire, testify to the relevance of the medieval founding of the monastery up until the end of the Baroque period.

58fa3a97-2ab3-5a6d-aeef-3f7f461c21ff.name: The Triumph of Peace and Justice
58fa3a97-2ab3-5a6d-aeef-3f7f461c21ff.description: The Triumph of Peace and Justice, with the flying figures of Justice, holding the fasces, and of Abundance, with the fruits.

5b66ccc1-4f4e-5e59-afac-9cb5613ba254.name: Staircase
5b66ccc1-4f4e-5e59-afac-9cb5613ba254.description: The Italian artists were part of the D. Martinelli circle, participating in the construction of the Liechtenstein palace in Vienna. The stucco artist, Bussi, also worked with Fischer von Erlach and J. L. Hildebrandt.

5e5ff728-46b9-5dbd-a88e-16ce672bc4f4.name: Chapel of the Holy Cross
5e5ff728-46b9-5dbd-a88e-16ce672bc4f4.description: A court architect who trained in Vienna and in Rome continued the construction of the chateau and completed the rectangular chapel in the south wing. The relief decorations, with the *Laying of Christ in His Grave* on the high altar, and the *Madonna of Old Brno* and the *Death of St. Francis* on side altars, were created by court sculptor Johann Stern, brother of the painter Josef Stern. The chapel portal, designed by Grimm, was executed by the Brno stonemason Joachim Günther.
5e5ff728-46b9-5dbd-a88e-16ce672bc4f4.artist: František Antonín Grimm (1710–1784, Brno), Johann Stern, Joachim Günther

6170eca7-efbd-5cb1-8474-f0ef9b1c591c.name: Carillons
6170eca7-efbd-5cb1-8474-f0ef9b1c591c.description: A Flanders-made ensemble of two carillons with 92 bells commissioned by King D. João V, representing the world’s largest historical set. The north tower carillon has 45 bells and the south tower carillon 47 bells. The bells are made of bronze and their total weight is 217 tons. According to tradition, when the king was told the astronomic price of only one carillon, he answered "I didn't expect it to be that cheap, I'll have two."

7015959d-b802-5549-a4a7-81818e774e68.name: *St. Joseph’s Dream*
7015959d-b802-5549-a4a7-81818e774e68.location: Altar painting, court chapel, Oršić Castle

724ecf67-8522-5e73-9afd-9978350e2c01.name: Hall of the Ancestors
724ecf67-8522-5e73-9afd-9978350e2c01.description:
Chancellor Václav Antonín completed reconstruction of a former garden room with a ceiling painting of the Gods on Mount Olympus and displayed larger-than-life portraits of his parents, grandparents and his wife.  
The Hall of the Ancestors is connected to the oval Historical Hall by illusionary painted architecture. It was here that the truce between Austria and France was signed after the Battle of Austerlitz.

767b259b-ec09-5677-98c7-f929983f4b2b.name: Drawing of  Pombaline Façades
767b259b-ec09-5677-98c7-f929983f4b2b.description:
Fire became a major concern after the earthquake of 1755 when tightly packed downtown Lisbon was consumed by fire that swept through the narrow streets and quickly destroyed buildings that were built closely together.  
Henceforth, buildings were separated by stone walls in order to isolate them. The uniform, multi-storey Pombaline façades (with shops, three domestic floors and an attic) are unique, constructed at a time when the focus was on safety and cost was a priority.  
The uniformity of the façades and windows is linked to the cost controls that dictated reconstruction: installation of the doors and windows were straightforward once all the stone frames had been made with identical measurements. The addition of a coat of arms was not allowed.

773672e7-c81d-5cd0-bedd-93bea7b36705.name: *Allegorical celebration of the thermal water in Porretta*
773672e7-c81d-5cd0-bedd-93bea7b36705.description: This painted decoration was created to celebrate the family by enhancing the therapeutic properties of the thermal water which springs in Porretta, a small village on the mountains around Bologna, a feud of the Ranuzzi from 1482. Girolamo Ranuzzi asked the poet Pier Jacopo Martello to create an iconographic programme to translate in painting. Vittorio Bigari and Stefano Orlandi painted the ceiling between 1724 and 1725.
773672e7-c81d-5cd0-bedd-93bea7b36705.location: Ceiling decoration of the so-called ‘Galleria’, Palazzo Ranuzzi

795a67c4-4c3c-5df0-8c64-eacfd926fc71.name: Main Chapel exterior
795a67c4-4c3c-5df0-8c64-eacfd926fc71.description: The element of surprise, a major component of the project, continues to impose itself on all those that walk the labyrinthine streets surrounding the cathedral.
795a67c4-4c3c-5df0-8c64-eacfd926fc71.artist: Johan Friedrich Ludwig (João Frederico Ludovice, active 1718–1746)

79ee1d89-b25b-54b7-9f77-22260ee5d520.name: Vault of the Grand Hall
79ee1d89-b25b-54b7-9f77-22260ee5d520.description: The vault is divided into four sections by diagonal strips. In between each section, there are round medallions with scenes from Roman military history, as well as emblems with the motifs of antique military equipment: shields, torches and flags.
79ee1d89-b25b-54b7-9f77-22260ee5d520.location: Second floor, Palace of the Sugar Refinery

7bfae956-1b6f-569b-bb35-b579c1e19ea0.name: View of the Choir
7bfae956-1b6f-569b-bb35-b579c1e19ea0.description: Interior with square bays of baldachin vaults.

8335d26b-5dea-5502-948b-ed9fdba57da6.name: *Ensemble d’époque*: Dining-Room
8335d26b-5dea-5502-948b-ed9fdba57da6.description: Like the bedroom, the re-creation of an 18th-century dining-room is located in the east wing of the palace. Again worthy of mention are the *azulejos* that line the walls depicting rural themes, romantic scenes and *chinoiseries* most of which date to 1746.

83a35999-406e-5ef3-a9b6-1e038d1d60e2.name: Three out of the six original plans with a new layout sympathetic to the old one; final plan and orthophoto of Lisbon
83a35999-406e-5ef3-a9b6-1e038d1d60e2.description: Following the earthquake of 1755, the Marquis of Pombal rapidly ordered a competition for the design of *Baixa Pombalina*. Six plans were submitted from which he would select the winner. On 4 December 1755, Manuel da Maia and Eugénio dos Santos presented plans that proposed replacing Terreiro do Paço (Palace Square) with Praça do Comércio, conceived as a monumental entrance into the town through the Cais das Colunas (Columns Quay).
83a35999-406e-5ef3-a9b6-1e038d1d60e2.artist: Military engineers: Manuel da Maia (1677–1766), Eugénio dos Santos (1711–1760)

83b6729d-7c75-5598-b935-15ef40ebd71d.name: Ancient Ruler
83b6729d-7c75-5598-b935-15ef40ebd71d.description: The impressive chateau entrance is rich in sculpted decoration. The bridge opens with sphinxes and the parapet is lined with vases with *putti*. The entrance gate is flanked by personifications of Strength and Power, symbolised by the mythological figure of Hercules and the figure of a ruler with the coat of arms of the investors. The gate pillars carry winged horses. The artistic ideas culminate in statues of ancient gods on the parapet: Hera, Zeus, Pallas Athene and Apollo, epitomising Good Government, Wisdom and the Arts (J. C. Pröbstl).

84149fe6-4a0e-5c7e-942e-8173633f866e.name: *Gaiolas* Building Structure
84149fe6-4a0e-5c7e-942e-8173633f866e.description: *The Gaiola Pombalina* is a remarkable symmetrical structure built from wood to distribute and balance the forces of an earthquake. All buildings in downtown Lisbon were built according to this system, and this is the world's first anti-seismic structure. This prototype, built by the fire department at the beginning of the 20th century, is used for fire-fighting training.
84149fe6-4a0e-5c7e-942e-8173633f866e.location: *Baixa Pombalina* or downtown Lisbon. These drawings are displayed in Museu da Cidade and a prototype is in the Museu dos Bombeiros.
84149fe6-4a0e-5c7e-942e-8173633f866e.artist: Eugénio dos Santos (1711–1760); Carlos Mardel (c. 1695–1763), Manuel da Maia (1677–1766)

86945764-6ee6-5a39-8aa8-6d6d98fb73a2.name: Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary
86945764-6ee6-5a39-8aa8-6d6d98fb73a2.description: Italian architects and stucco artists came to Moravia from royal service in Poland. In Valtice they created the first buildings in the early Baroque style. The original cupola on a drum, the first of its kind in Central Europe, was pulled down shortly after its completion due to its instability. Statues of saints were inserted into the church frontage, while the sculpted interior decoration gained importance dominated by heavy stuccowork. Artists participating in the decoration included G. da Cremona from Italy, the Flemish artist F. de Neve, I. Lengelacher and others.
86945764-6ee6-5a39-8aa8-6d6d98fb73a2.artist: Giovanni Battista Carlone I (before 1590–1645), Giovanni Giacomo Tencalla (c. 1600–c. 1650), Giovanni Tencalla, Giovanni Pietro Tencalla (1629 Bissone? – 1702 Vienna?)

89542836-1bd2-508a-9e55-b7f2185eb881.name: Monumental staircase
89542836-1bd2-508a-9e55-b7f2185eb881.description:
Around 1688 Annibale Ranuzzi commissioned the construction of a monumental staircase for his residential palace in Bologna. The presence of a monumental staircase was a very important element in the baroque ceremonies connected with Bolognese senatorial class political and social activities.  
It is not possible to identify the creator of the staircase. Some believe he must be identified with Giovanni Battista Torri, who paid for the wood model of the work. Others believe he must be identified with the famous Carlo Fontana, who was contacted by the patron together with other architects.  
The work was finished around 1695.
89542836-1bd2-508a-9e55-b7f2185eb881.artist: Giovanni Battista Torri (?), Carlo Fontana (?), Ercole Graziani; Filippo Balugani

89f1df55-2357-58fe-bc86-45fa395f58bf.name: The *Baptism of Christ*
89f1df55-2357-58fe-bc86-45fa395f58bf.description: The Baptism group, conceived as a counterpart to the pulpit, belongs among the major works of Swabian Rococo for, among other reasons, the sensitive gestures of the sculptures and the capricious form of the altar-like framing.
89f1df55-2357-58fe-bc86-45fa395f58bf.location: Northeast crossing pillar of the abbey church, above the baptismal font
89f1df55-2357-58fe-bc86-45fa395f58bf.artist: Johann Michael Feichtmayr (1696–1772); Johann Joseph Christian (1706–1777)

8c6e7a5a-f8b4-50cb-b4d1-b5bba30ca387.name: Dominik Ondřej Kounic with the Order of the Golden Fleece
8c6e7a5a-f8b4-50cb-b4d1-b5bba30ca387.description: The spur for the spectacular reconstruction of a Renaissance palace for the Kounic family came from Dominik Ondřej of Kounice, Imperial Vice-Chancellor. Kounic first commissioned the Bavarian architect Zuccali and later D. Martinelli, who had worked for the family in other parts of the demesne (Uherský Brod). Only the west wing was completed. The bust was created by Jan Blommendael, portraitist of William III Oranje-Nassau (Mauritshuis). Kounic stayed in the Hague during the peace negotiations that took place between 1695 and1697. He was also portrayed by Hyacinth Rigaud.

8ce1345f-9a1d-5d72-9553-3b644103bd1d.name: *Phlegmatic*
8ce1345f-9a1d-5d72-9553-3b644103bd1d.location: Wall of the working cabinet, Ratkaj Palace

8da4bfa4-102e-544c-8d43-38afff470b75.name: Congress hall
8da4bfa4-102e-544c-8d43-38afff470b75.description: The congress hall, as a second, far less intricately designed festive hall, was installed in the north wing and served as a counselling room. Its Rococo stuccowork on the ceiling was completed around 1758, in all likelihood by Franz Singer. The stucco is of extreme elegance and delicacy and lends the hall the character of an intimate chamber, which, while hardly in accordance with the original intention, reflects the declining political importance of the representatives of the estates.

8fa2cd8d-b816-515a-9e0d-d37d36b4f317.name: Ceiling fresco
8fa2cd8d-b816-515a-9e0d-d37d36b4f317.description: According to Gumpp’s plans the large hall was originally intended to be decorated exclusively with stucco, however this was abandoned. A competition was announced, which was won by Asam. The ceiling picture, largely depicting the glorification of the state of Tyrol and its various regions, was designed and painted by Asam according to a conceit from Stickler, the Abbot of Wilten.

9159ffdd-4a9a-524e-8b47-9e3d2e15912a.name: Plan of the Cathedral of St. Theresa, Požega
9159ffdd-4a9a-524e-8b47-9e3d2e15912a.description:
Late Baroque longitudinal, centralised type with curved lateral chapels  
positioned on a transversal axe.

9945fbfe-1d4b-5e33-a105-610f2f4a3994.name: Model of Lisbon before the earthquake of 1755
9945fbfe-1d4b-5e33-a105-610f2f4a3994.description: A large-scale model of Lisbon’s city centre before the earthquake of 1755.
9945fbfe-1d4b-5e33-a105-610f2f4a3994.artist: Gustavo Matos Cerqueira, Vieira da Silva and others

9d1b3ddb-6a64-5dc1-ae7b-afa6d1da6b9b.name: Exterior, east façade
9d1b3ddb-6a64-5dc1-ae7b-afa6d1da6b9b.description: The Hofburg’s main façade differs significantly from that facing the Hofgasse. The wing was erected between 1766–80 according to plans from Pacassi and under the direction of the Viennese military architect Constantin Walter von Pfeilsberg. Gumpp’s plan was abandoned in favour of a new conception. The elongated, lightly curved front is designed along the lines of the Viennese palace built at the same time. It has a high basement storey and colossal order, with two seven-axis portal projections and rounded corner pavilions composed of existing towers.

9dddcf81-e7ef-57de-826f-00c891445be3.name: Imaginary cityscape in the Salon with Panoramic Views
9dddcf81-e7ef-57de-826f-00c891445be3.description: The wall paintings of imaginary cityscapes reveal the influence of the architectural drawings of Giovanni Battista Piranesi.
9dddcf81-e7ef-57de-826f-00c891445be3.location: Second floor, west salon, Palace of the Sugar Refinery

a141a2a7-c77e-5121-9c0d-10970929fb2e.name: Chateau design
a141a2a7-c77e-5121-9c0d-10970929fb2e.description: The design followed an existing building which on the north side was to be flanked by ground-floor side-wings ending in prismatic constructions. The main frontage is made more striking by a protruding circular hall. Older fortifications prevented the completion of all but the east wing. The “correspondence plan” from the royal court architect in Paris was adjusted to local conditions by the builder Ludwig Sebastian Kaltner.
a141a2a7-c77e-5121-9c0d-10970929fb2e.artist: Robert de Cotte (1656–1735, Paris), Ludwig Sebastian Kaltner

a1ef0742-6721-5a62-b45f-58953a49f528.name: Ceremonial courtyard
a1ef0742-6721-5a62-b45f-58953a49f528.description: The completion of the residence was chiefly an urban logistical task. The outbuildings were already standing in the 17th century, as well as a riding hall on the right and a theatre on the left. The style of the Viennese engineer and decorator A. J. Ospel, followed in the footsteps of F. Borromini and F. G. Galli-Bibiena. The contrast between simple shapes and impressive stonemasonry detail is typical of the artist. The majority of Ospel’s works for the chateau interiors have not survived (for example, an elaborate ceramic stove). The space opens with telamons by G. Giuliani.
a1ef0742-6721-5a62-b45f-58953a49f528.artist: Ondřej Erna, Jan Křtitel Erna, Anton Josef Ospel (1677–1756)

a510d0cb-7ef9-570d-8610-ec9568ed5fcb.name: Celebration of Emperor Charles VI
a510d0cb-7ef9-570d-8610-ec9568ed5fcb.description:
Governor Kounic was a follower of Charles VI and a promoter of the “pragmatic sanction”. He systematically addressed the modernisation of the country and reforms in public administration. With the emperor’s support Kounic unified the administration and the royal tribunal into a Provincial Governorate, which spurred the construction of a new entrance wing by M. Grimm, its central bay with two passageways symbolising the new office. The staircase and the new Assembly Hall were decorated by local artists.  
The artist, F. Ř. I. Eckstein also tendered for the commission to decorate the Assembly Hall but he was spurned and left Brno to work for the Jesuits in Lviv where he later died.
a510d0cb-7ef9-570d-8610-ec9568ed5fcb.artist: František Řehoř Ignác Eckstein (1689? Židovice u Žatce – 1741 Lviv)

aad909a1-b106-56bf-86ee-b7aee4a41eef.name: Central ceiling fresco in the Riesensaal
aad909a1-b106-56bf-86ee-b7aee4a41eef.description: The painted ceiling, including the painted stucco, covers an area of c. 500 square metres and is one of Franz Anton Maulbertsch’s major works. The empress personally contributed to its design. The central fresco shows an allegory of the union of the royal houses of Austria and Lorraine, the flanking ovals depict the regalia of Tyrol. The marriage of the houses of Austria and Lorraine is depicted as a chariot, accompanied by personifications of the sovereign’s virtues.

add54831-b132-5b1c-9ed1-5c4eec59a759.name: Praça do Comércio
add54831-b132-5b1c-9ed1-5c4eec59a759.description: Praça do Comércio overlooking the River Tejo is an emblematic part of the *Baixa*. According to the engraving attributed to Gaspar Froes Machado, the initial plans were not entirely fulfilled; the triumphal arch was finally built in 1873 according to the design of Veríssimo José da Costa.
add54831-b132-5b1c-9ed1-5c4eec59a759.location: Facing the estuary of the River Tagus
add54831-b132-5b1c-9ed1-5c4eec59a759.artist: Initial plans of Praça do Comércio: Manuel da Maia (1677–1766), Eugénio dos Santos (1711–1760); Carlos Mardel (c. 1695–1763); triumphal arch: Veríssimo José da Costa [n.d.] assisted by Vítor Bastos (1830–1894) and Anatole C. Calmels (1822–1906)

ae77a293-7b0e-5067-bde6-8ea3bbcc4d01.name: *Ensemble d’époque*: Bedroom
ae77a293-7b0e-5067-bde6-8ea3bbcc4d01.description: Installed in the east wing facing the Buxo Garden is a re-creation of an 18th-century bedroom. It is worth mentioning in particular the *azulejos* that line the walls depicting rural themes, romantic scenes and chinoiseries most of which date to 1746.

b1a77da8-c428-593d-a327-c702cc601914.name: Staircase
b1a77da8-c428-593d-a327-c702cc601914.description: A staircase of great scale and ostentation it is fixed in the nucleus of the palace.
b1a77da8-c428-593d-a327-c702cc601914.location: Interior of the palace, Pimenta Palace

b3dc84c7-1930-5b07-b085-55d198c770fa.name: St. Vincent and St. Sebastian
b3dc84c7-1930-5b07-b085-55d198c770fa.description: Depicting the Martyrs St. Sebastian and St. Vincent, these sculptures represent just two pieces from The Royal Commission, which includes among other precious items 56 Italian sculptures, representing the most important collection of Italian Baroque sculpture outside Italy. The two sculptures illustrated here are made from marble; each one is 3.58-meters tall.

b4d6753b-ee3a-5120-a57e-e35af32589c1.name: Hall of the Ancestors
b4d6753b-ee3a-5120-a57e-e35af32589c1.description: The monumental and technically demanding building on an unusual elliptical ground plan, celebrates a Swabian-Bavarian dynasty that settled in Moravia in the second half of the 16th century. Statues in the niches represent real and mythical family figures. Erlach followed in the footsteps of Bernini in the design. The memorial building changed function in the mid-18th century when the Hall, with its pre-Romanticism terraces, became a viewing point for surveying the beautiful countryside around the chateau.
b4d6753b-ee3a-5120-a57e-e35af32589c1.artist: Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach (1656 Graz – 1723 Vienna), Tobias Kracker (1658–1736, Vienna)

b7aa2d97-f660-5f39-a7c3-53ec68eec878.name: Victory Hall
b7aa2d97-f660-5f39-a7c3-53ec68eec878.description: The Regency-style panelled hall shows in its paintings, reliefs, concave moulding and ceiling fresco scenes of war, which refer to the Elector’s military success in the Turkish Wars. Scenes of the unsuccessful War of the Spanish Succession were deliberately avoided.
b7aa2d97-f660-5f39-a7c3-53ec68eec878.location: New Palace, first floor of the central wing
b7aa2d97-f660-5f39-a7c3-53ec68eec878.artist: Johann Adam Pichler (c. 1690–1761); Charles Dubut (c. 1687–1742): Jacopo Amigoni (c. 1682–1752); Joachim Beich (1665–1748)

b83ce496-5956-54df-b73a-f5033db4841f.name: The Twelve Tablets of the Law
b83ce496-5956-54df-b73a-f5033db4841f.description: The Hall, containing the provincial tablets of the law, is decorated with scenes featuring *Emperor Ferdinand II*, *Moses' Decalogue*, the *Defence of the Provincial Tablets* and the *Guardians of the Public Trust*, represented by the figures of an aristocrat, a clergyman and a burgher, as well as a scrivener. The tablets, introduced in 1348, were a code of law that preceded the [land books](http://cs.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pozemkov%C3%A1_kniha "Pozemková kniha") where all enactments of [provincial assemblies](http://cs.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zemsk%C3%BD_sn%C4%9Bm&action=edit "Zemský snem") were recorded. [Joseph II's](http://cs.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josef_II. "Josef II.") reform of [1783](http://cs.wikipedia.org/wiki/1783 "1783") abolished the tablets' office, and legal authority passed to the new provincial court. *Leges XII tabularum*, written according to tradition in 450, formulated Roman consuetudinary law. The interpretation of its regulations laid the foundations of continental legal science, while the interpretation of its ancient language provided a basis for philology.

b985235f-025a-5eed-a7b8-96646d281fd8.name: The Triumph of Religion and Spirituality
b985235f-025a-5eed-a7b8-96646d281fd8.description: The Triumph of Religion and Spirituality, where Science, holding a book on the one hand and fire on the other, gazes at the Heaven above, the true source of knowledge. Down next to her, Religion holding a tripod.

b9abc8a0-1fc1-59ad-9b41-3194b57afd27.name: Throne Room
b9abc8a0-1fc1-59ad-9b41-3194b57afd27.description: The Throne Room, also known as the Great Room, is the largest of the palace's three state rooms. Construction began in 1768 when the marriage of Dom Pedro to the future Queen Maria I demanded a large area for official audiences. Designed by the architect, Jean-Baptiste Robillion, the new room was built in the Rococo style with carvings by the sculptor and wood carver, Silvestre de Faria Lobo. The paintings on the ceiling represent Faith, Sun, Hope, War, Justice and Charity and were executed under the direction of the painter, João de Freitas Leitão. Manuel da Costa, António Berardi and Manuel do Nascimento assisted him.
b9abc8a0-1fc1-59ad-9b41-3194b57afd27.artist: Jean Baptiste Robillion (active 1758–1782); carving: Silvestre de Faria Lobo; painters: João de Freitas Leitão, Manuel da Costa, António Berardi, Manuel do Nascimento, whose dates are unknown.

bad50899-194a-53f5-8b17-f81567ff0b42.name: High altar
bad50899-194a-53f5-8b17-f81567ff0b42.description: The bundle of columns of the powerful main altar made of stucco marble forms an imposing frame for the topics of the altarpiece, namely the Trinity and Redemption. To the sides, larger-than-life stucco figures of the apostles Peter and Paul in ecstatically-moved depictions admonish the faithful, while respectively, the painting reflects on the secret of faith. On either side are the figures of the holy bishops Ulrich and Conrad, both of whom were patrons of the Swabian bishoprics of Augsburg and Konstanz.
bad50899-194a-53f5-8b17-f81567ff0b42.artist: Johann Michael Feichtmayr (1696–1772); Johann Joseph Christian (1706–1777); Johann Jakob Zeiller (1708–1783)

bbb068e0-786d-5185-ae89-0a937e547d94.name: Ceiling fresco of the Dining Room
bbb068e0-786d-5185-ae89-0a937e547d94.description: The enchanting fresco on the ceiling of the Dining Room shows Odysseus’ arrival at the nymph Calypso’s island guarded in heaven by gods. It was painted primarily during the reign of Max III Joseph.
bbb068e0-786d-5185-ae89-0a937e547d94.location: New Palace, ground floor of the central wing

bbf2ac31-f420-5547-903d-485e39009fa1.name: Arches over the Alcântara valley
bbf2ac31-f420-5547-903d-485e39009fa1.description: The structure uses the pointed arch in some of the larger arches crossing the Alcântara valley. Curiously, some of the stones of the Aqueduct are inscribed with the masons' initials, a custom that was all but lost but which was revived here.

bc51144d-7f51-569b-98c3-5440f70f3532.name: Ceiling stucco in the vestibule of the large summer dining hall
bc51144d-7f51-569b-98c3-5440f70f3532.description: The rich ornamentation consists of strapwork, grids, bells and festoons of flowers. G. M. Fontana came from a large north-Italian family active in Moravia from the 1660s. He also worked on the decoration of the chateau frontage. The room originally featured tapestries with scenes by P. Brueghel Sr.

bf8d5dd6-621c-537a-a14f-13c5c7464cea.name: Gardens
bf8d5dd6-621c-537a-a14f-13c5c7464cea.description: Expansion of the garden was possible after resolution of the uneven land quotas and the relatively rough excavation. The garden's first designer was the Dutchman, Jan van der Kolke, who followed the plans of Robillion. The expansion followed a structure typical of the Portuguese “farm”, purchasing the surrounding land to create a formal garden, a recreational garden and a large area for cultivation, the *Quinta Real*.
bf8d5dd6-621c-537a-a14f-13c5c7464cea.artist: Jean Baptiste Robillion (active 1758–1782); Garden statues: John Cheere (1709-1787)

c033a142-ba63-5940-81e3-bdf3db2aed83.name: *Allegories of the Four Seasons, Four Temperaments and Four Elements*
c033a142-ba63-5940-81e3-bdf3db2aed83.description: Four allegories representing the Four Seasons, the Four Stages of Life, the Four Elements, Four Tempers and, finally, the Four Senses, painted by Anton Jožef Lerchinger after prints by Johann Georg Bergmüller (Turkheim, Schwaben 1688 – Augsburg 1762) from Augsburg.
c033a142-ba63-5940-81e3-bdf3db2aed83.location: Wall of the working cabinet, Ratkaj Palace

c2794ae5-2bd4-58c8-894b-a8fbe7024d22.name: Oršić Castle, Central Hall Frescoes
c2794ae5-2bd4-58c8-894b-a8fbe7024d22.description: *Trompe l'œil* window frescos articulate the walls of the Central hall. Within the windows are painted landscapes.

c27eb774-cc9f-55db-b3e3-343e34b005f2.name: Middle room balcony railings
c27eb774-cc9f-55db-b3e3-343e34b005f2.description: Each room has a different colour scheme and decorative emphasis with multicoloured bookshelves of different lacquered finishes in green, red and black decorated with *chinoiserie* motifs. Each of the rooms is two-storeys high, with a balcony and stairs incorporated into the furniture.
c27eb774-cc9f-55db-b3e3-343e34b005f2.location: Interior, Biblioteca Joanina da Universidade de Coimbra
c27eb774-cc9f-55db-b3e3-343e34b005f2.artist: Design and execution: Francesco Gualdini, João Rodrigues de Almeida; supervisor: Gaspar Ferreira; painting and gilding of woodwork: Manuel da Silva [dates unknown]

c2fbeb88-8a77-582a-a431-c3d1fbc93542.name: Main fresco
c2fbeb88-8a77-582a-a431-c3d1fbc93542.description: The nave frescos of the monastery church are typologically woven into one another, depicting the life of the founder of the Cistercian Order, Bernhard of Clairvaux, and likewise, the Life of Christ. Using the solemnity of the church year from west to east the position of the Cistercians within God’s divine plan for salvation is accented: the Birth of Christ and Saint Bernhard’s vision of it; the Resurrection with its sermon for the Duke of Aquitaine; the Ascent to Heaven with the entrance of the saint into the Citeaux Monastery as well as the despatch of the Holy Ghost with Bernhard’s visions of Christ Crucified and the Virgin Mary.

c4949ddb-d9d5-551d-b5df-1849fe2e8307.name: Ceremonial Façade (main façade)
c4949ddb-d9d5-551d-b5df-1849fe2e8307.description: Perhaps one of the best palace façades of the Portuguese Baroque, it combines traditional Portuguese features with Classical precision. The triangular pediment, adorned at the tympanum with garlands, averts the solemnity of a façade which is the keynote of the garden views.
c4949ddb-d9d5-551d-b5df-1849fe2e8307.location: Exterior view from the Pênsil Garden
c4949ddb-d9d5-551d-b5df-1849fe2e8307.artist: Jean Baptiste Robillion (active 1758–1782), Mateus Vicente de Oliveira (1706–1786)

c9e437ac-0abc-54f8-bdb1-c612628c79a0.name: Celebration of the Althann Dynasty
c9e437ac-0abc-54f8-bdb1-c612628c79a0.description: Illusionary elements of a balustrade and carpet provide a link between the earth and the celestial sphere. Ancient gods and allegorical figures show a path to honour and glory. The family’s celestial triumph is accompanied by scenes depicting aristocratic virtues. The major component is not stuccowork but painting, in contrast to more recent decorations. The fresco as one of the first pieces by an artist who later became famous.

cc3d0593-4799-50e0-9f3d-44bc2af39e0e.name: Staircase
cc3d0593-4799-50e0-9f3d-44bc2af39e0e.description: The Imperial-style staircase has three flights. It bears characteristics typical of the 1780s, consisting of superimposed columns, strips and cornices originally painted in a marble paint finish, while the railing has a decorative motif of a square meander, which also points to the Early Classical language of architecture.
cc3d0593-4799-50e0-9f3d-44bc2af39e0e.location: Central area (opposite the entrance hall), Palace of the Sugar Refinery

d0ab1550-cbd5-5935-b8c4-fe0633742da9.name: Neptune Fountain
d0ab1550-cbd5-5935-b8c4-fe0633742da9.description: The Neptune Fountain is perhaps one of the most remarkable pieces of 17th-century Baroque stonework in Portugal. Originating during the period of the Castelo Melhor, the fountain was commissioned in Rome shortly after 1675 , 1675 by Luis de Meneses, Count of Ericeira and Portuguese Ambassador in Rome, and made specifically for his Lisbon palace of Anunciada where it was installed in the gardens. After the earthquake of 1755, the fountain fell into the hands of other owners and ended up in several different locations. It was finally purchased by the state and placed in the gardens of Queluz in the first half of the 20th century. Today we know it was probably commissioned from Gian Lorenzo Bernini (the *“vernino*” as he is referred to in Portuguese documentation) who delegated work on it to Ercole Ferrata.

d1c1eb40-6c20-5043-8872-8d70084736b5.name: *Pastoral theme*
d1c1eb40-6c20-5043-8872-8d70084736b5.location: Wall of the working cabinet, Ratkaj Palace

d2a0bb6d-e271-5430-bd69-fba3a45eaf85.name:
Bronze Equestrian Statue of King José I  
(copper engraving by Carneiro da Silva made before the unveiling in 1774)
d2a0bb6d-e271-5430-bd69-fba3a45eaf85.description: The statue by Joaquim Machado de Castro was unveiled on 27 May 1775 on King José I’s birthday. The copper engraving by Joaquim Carneiro da Silva was made a year prior to this in 1774 to commemorate the unveiling. Other commemorative items include china decorated with reproductions of the statue.
d2a0bb6d-e271-5430-bd69-fba3a45eaf85.location: Terreiro do Paço (Palace Square) or Praça do Comércio (Commerce  Square)

d2aaaa35-322e-55c8-aa9a-d4c8876f0303.name: Staircase
d2aaaa35-322e-55c8-aa9a-d4c8876f0303.description: The wide, double flight of stairs is the first monumental Baroque staircase in Innsbruck. From the vestibule on the ground floor it leads upwards to the first and second floors. The rich stucco ornamentation in the form of Baroque strapwork originates from Anton Gigl, Johann Singer, Paul Wachter and Andreas Gratl, the sculptures in the niches of the round arches on the second floor are from Nikolaus Moll (Apollo and Artemis) and Ingenium Lechleitner (busts of Zeus and Hera). On the ceiling in front of the parliament hall Lechleitner also depicted the map of Tyrol in stucco, supported by an eagle, the state’s heraldic animal.
d2aaaa35-322e-55c8-aa9a-d4c8876f0303.location: Main wing, connection between first and second floors
d2aaaa35-322e-55c8-aa9a-d4c8876f0303.artist: Georg Anton Gumpp (1682–1754); Nikolaus Moll (1676–1754); Ingenuin Lechleitner (1676–1731); Anton Gigl (1700–1769); Johann Singer [n.d.]

d57919ad-92e5-5973-9707-042b48266da3.name: Mercury
d57919ad-92e5-5973-9707-042b48266da3.description: The chateau frontage is segmented by windows and niches with statues – allegories of the seasons and figures of ancient gods.
d57919ad-92e5-5973-9707-042b48266da3.artist: Jan Jirí Schauberger (? before 1725 Vienna, active in Olomouc – 1744 Brno)

d5bb0a84-dc09-524d-955d-6f8930019c18.name: Chapel
d5bb0a84-dc09-524d-955d-6f8930019c18.description: The fresco of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary is one of the lesser-known works of renowned Viennese master, Mildorfer. A sketch for the painting is preserved in the Reuschel Collection in Munich. Cartouches contain *putti* with symbols of St. John of Nepomuk.

d6106d67-8053-5953-b8d3-21dcd5e36a0d.name: Mãe d’ Água das Amoreiras reservoir
d6106d67-8053-5953-b8d3-21dcd5e36a0d.description: Mãe d' Água das Amoreiras reservoir was designed by Carlos Mardel. Due to its monumentality, the Mãe d'Água constitutes a true civic temple to the *águas livres* (free waters). An antechamber precedes the vast rectangle which contains a deep reservoir.

d6a6bbee-1004-5fe5-93a3-c845fe7b8380.name: Library
d6a6bbee-1004-5fe5-93a3-c845fe7b8380.description:
A significant Enlightenment Library with around 36,000 volumes amassed through royal commission. It has a cruciform layout with a multi-coloured limestone floor and Rocaille shelves.  
Some rare works furnish its shelves to this day: the *Nuremberg Chronicle* (1493) or the *Theatrvm Orbis Terrarvm* by Ortelius (1595) and a nucleus of scores from musicians such as João de Sousa Carvalho or Marcos Portugal, composed expressly to be played on the Basilica's six organs.

d8289a89-1170-5ec0-a741-c5175017f870.name: Chapel of the Holy Trinity
d8289a89-1170-5ec0-a741-c5175017f870.description: This chateau chapel, with a subterranean family tomb, is a conceptual and compositional counterpart to the Hall of the Ancestors. The cylindrical central nave, with six oval apses around the perimeter, is decorated with paintings – the Last Judgment, Heaven and Paradise – drawing attention to the ephemeral nature of existence, the end of human life and its continuation in eternity. The cupola fresco represents the Archangel Michael, the family’s patron saint and protector of the Church.
d8289a89-1170-5ec0-a741-c5175017f870.artist: Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach (1656 Graz – 1723 Vienna), Ignaz Heinitz of Heintzenthal (1657–1742, Vienna)

d91846ba-1200-5b0a-820b-a4e5e1687ce1.name: *Ensemble d’époque*: Kitchen
d91846ba-1200-5b0a-820b-a4e5e1687ce1.description: Re-creation of an 18th-century kitchen set up in what was the original palace kitchen. Lined with *azulejos* (tile panels) of random figures alluding to culinary themes (for example, a bad cook and hanging game), it is equipped with a wide-mouthed chimney, stone tables and contemporary kitchen utensils.

d9da836f-3e6b-5c2a-b9e8-6a9d2289580c.name: Main façade
d9da836f-3e6b-5c2a-b9e8-6a9d2289580c.description: The façade facing Maria-Theresien-Straße forms the buildings’ main, monumental visible side. Modelled on the scheme of the Palazzo Chigi Odescalchi in Rome, only the central projection is distinguished by colossal pilasters, a massive temple-like front elevated above the rusticated ground floor. The central projection is extended by a mezzanine storey and flanked by three-storey sections whose horizontal plane is augmented by powerful mouldings. The central Borrominian window enriches the austere, massive design with flowing forms. The design of the façade clearly expresses combativeness and sovereign dignity.

dbaffd3f-8c80-55c5-8dff-c3db51a61236.name: Courtyard
dbaffd3f-8c80-55c5-8dff-c3db51a61236.description: Countess Marie Anna Pignatelli took up the reconstruction of the residence after 1722. She commissioned the court architect A. E. Martinelli to build a three-wing chateau, adjust the entrance bridge, parts of the castle front, and the chapel frontage and interior. The two-shouldered staircase of the ceremonial courtyard is set with sculptures of Hercules fighting Antaios and Aeneas Rescuing his Father, Anchises, from Burning Troy.

e83f959c-c5a5-5804-9244-9b13dbf232e5.name: Imperial Hall
e83f959c-c5a5-5804-9244-9b13dbf232e5.description: The architectonic and artificial painting arrangement of the ceremonial hall celebrates the idea and dignity of the Holy Roman Empire as well as the fidelity to the empire and the potential sovereignty of the abbey. The ceiling fresco shows the Coronation of Emperor Charlemagne in 800; four pictures to the sides describe the empire's functions in relation to its services for the church: *Ecclesiae propagatori* (propagator of the Church), *Ecclesiae propugnatori* (defender of the Church), *Hostium debellatori* (combatant against enemies) and *Scientiae fautori* (patron of science). Larger-than-life statues of the last 16 emperors, placed in front of the pompous columns of the wall decoration, show respectful reverence to the ruling House of Habsburg.
e83f959c-c5a5-5804-9244-9b13dbf232e5.location: Central projection of the west wing (3rd floor), Benedictine Abbey of St. Theodor and Alexander
e83f959c-c5a5-5804-9244-9b13dbf232e5.artist: Andrea Maini (b. 1683); Jakob Karl Stauder (1694–1751/56); Franz Anton Sturm (1690–1757)

e93c0684-321e-58c9-b7f4-2505ffdc37b6.name: Playing Putti
e93c0684-321e-58c9-b7f4-2505ffdc37b6.description: In the side lunettes of the Room of Fortune are depicted playing putti.
e93c0684-321e-58c9-b7f4-2505ffdc37b6.location: Ceiling decoration of a room of the first floor of the palace, detail, Palazzo Ranuzzi

eb2c6bd8-523c-5da1-ab39-330d09fffdc5.name: The Triumph of Intelligence over Brutality
eb2c6bd8-523c-5da1-ab39-330d09fffdc5.description: The Triumph of Intelligence, represented as Minerva, over Brutality, symbolized by the Giants.

eb503e88-060a-52e9-9182-c489847066be.name: Frontage
eb503e88-060a-52e9-9182-c489847066be.description: The portal to the third courtyard of the residence lends emphasis to the central section: the main hall, chapel and the count’s quarters, the oldest part of the complex. The count would greet his subjects from the balcony. Beduzzi’s decoration of the frontage was part of the second phase of the reconstruction; he was also responsible for some of the iconography of the residence. Beduzzi designed the sculpted decoration of the chateau and chapel interiors.
eb503e88-060a-52e9-9182-c489847066be.artist: Antonio Maria Nicolao Beduzzi (1675 Bologna – 1735 Vienna)

eb7a0351-f4ca-5902-b8bb-572d211a56e6.name: Carmo Fountain
eb7a0351-f4ca-5902-b8bb-572d211a56e6.description: From the Mãe d' Água das Amoreiras reservoir, a secondary aqueduct spreads out around the city terminating in fountains, many of them like this one still extant. Built by the engineer, Miguel Ângelo Blasco in 1769, it was redesigned by Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos in 1786.
eb7a0351-f4ca-5902-b8bb-572d211a56e6.artist: Attributed to the engineer, Miguel Ângelo Blasco (1769–1770) and the architect, Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos [n.d.]

ec147545-1850-5a97-9755-1387bdc2cc89.name: *Celebration of the Serényi family*
ec147545-1850-5a97-9755-1387bdc2cc89.description: The spectacular rectangular hall, referred to as the large summer dining hall, spans two storeys. The subject of wall and ceiling frescos is the triumph of the imperial army in the struggle against the Turks at the turn of the 17th century. The illusionary architecture blends with portraits of family members: Jan Karel Serényi (d.1691) took part in the victorious Siege of Vienna in 1683 and became a Commander-in-Chief in Munich. The figure of Hercules enthroned and the depictions of his deeds in the presence of ancient gods, along with the allegories of the Arts and Sciences, celebrate the military past and aristocratic nobility of the family. Above Jan Karel, András Serényi (d.1345) with allegories of Victory and Eternal Fame is depicted. The central figure is Emperor Charles VI portrayed as Apollo, surrounded by the Zodiac, Aurora, Luna and Chronos. The painter pays tribute to the family in his self-portrait. He is seen pointing to the Baptism of an Aristocrat, a scene that illustrates a family legend about an ancestor from a noble family of Hungarian origin known as Temnurtus (“The Dark”), who was baptised in 965 and adopted the name Serenus (“The Powerful”). Representations of Habsburg sovereigns, Czech kings and ancient rulers supplement the celebration of the Serényi family. Family history and its mythologization are major iconographic elements in Baroque residences.
ec147545-1850-5a97-9755-1387bdc2cc89.artist: František Ignác Řehoř Eckstein (1689 Židovice – 1741 Lviv)

ed2e5596-037a-5738-8eaa-d795beb82ba9.name: High Altar
ed2e5596-037a-5738-8eaa-d795beb82ba9.description:
The sculptor, António Bellini of Pádua, was responsible for the decoration of the chancel. He endowed it with a sense of immateriality and a subtle notion of “suspension” seen in, for example, the main altar where angels worship on top of the white marble pediment flanking the cedar sculpture of Christ by Manuel Dias.  
In the central panel is the *Assumption of the Virgin*, signed and dated 1731 by Agostino Masucci. This is surrounded by other paintings of the *Nativity,* *Conception*, *Adoration of the Shepherds* and the *Coronation,* all of which were painted in his workshop.
ed2e5596-037a-5738-8eaa-d795beb82ba9.artist: The angels, the *Four Virtues*, the pediment over the main arch and busts of *St. Peter and St. Paul* are by João António Bellini de Pádua (active 1725–1748); the paintings are by the workshop of Agostino Masucci

f7450b1c-6382-5c9c-a528-e4c11c55aa74.name: Ideal design for the residence
f7450b1c-6382-5c9c-a528-e4c11c55aa74.description: Martinelli’s design for reconstruction included the development of a major part of the town and a new parish church. The chateau, on a U-shaped ground plan with a ceremonial courtyard, reflected the status of the investor who thus laid the foundations for the future ambitions of the dynasty. The building director, Petruzzi, adjusted the design to local conditions, paying attention in particular to new functions and taste in accordance with a design by I. Valmaggini, later a building director in Vienna. Maxmilián Kounic, son of Dominik Ondřej and Secretary to Charles VI as well as a secret councillor, became a provincial governor and preferred a more austere design in the French style. The design included the segmentation of the garden with pools, parterres and mazes.

fb2c16ce-05ab-5038-b941-2740a8a0e2cb.name: Detail of ceiling painting
fb2c16ce-05ab-5038-b941-2740a8a0e2cb.description: The *Trompe l'oeil* ceiling painting depicts three manifestations of Wisdom: an allegory of the library (*Bibliotheca*), of the university (*Universitas*) and of the encyclopaedia (*Encyclopaedia*).
fb2c16ce-05ab-5038-b941-2740a8a0e2cb.location: Interior, Biblioteca Joanina da Universidade de Coimbra
fb2c16ce-05ab-5038-b941-2740a8a0e2cb.artist: António Simões Ribeiro and Vicente Nunes [n.d.]

fb3fdb2d-573f-563d-9108-61663265d16a.name: Portrait of João V
fb3fdb2d-573f-563d-9108-61663265d16a.description: The portrait of the King João V emerges from a sort of a “*rideau de scène*” in carved wood, upheld by angels. The oil on canvas painting is by Domenico Duprà, royal painter in Lisbon before 1730.
fb3fdb2d-573f-563d-9108-61663265d16a.location: Interior, Biblioteca Joanina da Universidade de Coimbra
